title: TRACE: Data-Free Text Reconstruction Attacks against Approximate Unlearning in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2610.31995v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) face growing demands for data removal driven by regulatory compliance, copyright concerns, and privacy protection, approximate unlearning has emerged as a practical alternative to expensive full retraining. In practice, pre- and post-unlearning model snapshots are often maintained for auditing and rollback, introducing a previously overlooked side channel. This paper demonstrates that approximate unlearning in LLM can leave residual traces within model snapshots, which may be recoverable and thus enable the privacy breaches that approximate unlearning is intended to prevent. Here, we propose TRACE, a framework that reconstructs unlearned training data given access to pre- and post-unlearning model snapshots, without any data-specific prior knowledge. translated_title: TRACE：针对大语言模型近似遗忘的免数据文本重建攻击
translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型（LLM）面临由法规合规、版权问题和隐私保护所驱动的日益增长的数据删除需求，近似遗忘已成为替代代价高昂的完全重训练的一种实用方案。在实践中，遗忘前后的模型快照通常会被保留用于审计和回滚，这引入了一个此前被忽视的侧信道。本文证明，大语言模型中的近似遗忘会在模型快照中留下残留痕迹，这些痕迹可能被恢复，从而导致近似遗忘本欲防范的隐私泄露。在此，我们提出TRACE框架，它能够在获得遗忘前后模型快照访问权限的条件下，无需任何数据特定的先验知识即可重建被遗忘的训练数据。为实现这一目标，TRACE从嵌入层级的参数差异中识别出一小部分候选词元以约束搜索空间，并组装……
tldr: 本文提出TRACE框架，利用遗忘前后的模型快照差异，在无需先验知识的情况下重建大语言模型中被近似遗忘的训练数据，揭示了模型快照所引入的隐私泄露侧信道风险。
en_tdlr: TRACE reconstructs unlearned training data in LLMs using only pre- and post-unlearning model snapshots without any prior knowledge, revealing that approximate unlearning leaves recoverable residual traces that create a previously overlooked privacy side channel.
